title: Increasing App Engagement Behaviors via Goal-Enabling Technology Features: The Role of Goal Difficulty Dimensions
eligible_reason: Staggered adoption of a binary app feature, but estimated with staggered synthetic control (Ben-Michael, Feller, Rothstein 2022) feeding a hierarchical heterogeneous-treatment-effect model with an IV control-function; no TWFE or CS/BJS specification.
design_notes: Investment app that introduced goal-enabling technology features (GETF); customers adopt at different times. Step 1: staggered synthetic control constructs a counterfactual for each adopter using customers who adopt later (holdout window) as donor pool, weights chosen on L = 21 pre-adoption periods. Step 2: hierarchical model of customer-level treatment effects as a function of goal-difficulty dimensions, with an IV-based control function. Plus a field experiment. Never-adopters are discarded. Synthetic control, matching on pre-period outcomes, IV and hierarchical Bayesian modeling are all excluded by the protocol.
screener_notes: Not eligible: synthetic control + IV + hierarchical model. Data statement: alternative disclosure plan; data not available, code and simulated data requestable through JMR Dataverse doi 10.7910/DVN/CJDOEZ. Screened from article text only.
